root_idea.summary: The root centers on coloring or altering a thing by applying a color.
root_idea.development: From literal coloring, the lexicon extends to dipping or immersion and to things marked or changed through contact. In the Quranic expressions, صِبْغ denotes a food dip or seasoning, while صِبْغَةُ الله presents religious identity or divinely given disposition through the metaphor of dye permeating a garment.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun with a distinct food-seasoning usage.
Quran-attested noun with a distinct religious and baptismal interpretation.

senses.definition: A sauce, condiment, or relish in which food is dipped, especially a fluid seasoning such as olive oil or vinegar.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ (23:20), the noun denotes a food accompaniment. It is interpreted specifically as olive oil or the olive in some explanations, while the broader lexical usage is a fluid seasoning or dip.

senses.definition: Religion or a God-given religious disposition and identity; the divinely prescribed way or faith by which a person is marked and brought near to God.
senses.usage_conditions: In صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ (2:138), the expression is explained as God's religion, fitrah, religious law, or what God has prescribed. Some explanations identify the prescribed mark specifically as circumcision. The dye image describes a quality that becomes manifest in, or permeates, the person who possesses it.

senses.definition: Baptism or ritual immersion as a religious marking; by extension, God's conferral of faith understood as a baptism unlike the Christian baptism.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative Quran-focused interpretation of صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ (2:138), based on the use of صِبْغَة for baptism or the mode of immersion by which a child is admitted to a religious community. It is an interpretive reading of the Quranic construction, not a claim that the verse has only this meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dye or color a thing, thereby altering its color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of garments, cloth, hair, and similar objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To moisten food with oil, grease, or sauce, or to dip or immerse an object in liquid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions for dipping a mouthful, hand, arm, or other object in a liquid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To baptize or ritually initiate a child by immersion into a religious community.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported particularly of Christian baptism and also of introducing a child into the Jewish community; this is a derived religious use of immersion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To color, alter, or embellish information or discourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use applied to changing the presentation of reported information or speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alter a person's standing in another's estimation, or, in a disputed idiom, to point someone out as capable of fulfilling a desired task.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The latter idiomatic report is explicitly rejected by one authority as a confusion with صَبَعَ; it is retained as a disputed Classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To work in a field of knowledge or in a craft and become notable through it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with knowledge, a branch of knowledge, or work as the field in which someone becomes accomplished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become full, extended, or ample, with a related improvement in appearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a camel's udder becoming full and goodly in color, a man's muscle becoming long, or a garment becoming long and ample.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put the head into food or pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to camels putting their heads into food, herbage, or pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dye garments thoroughly or repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intensive form can indicate muchness or repeated application of dye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin to ripen or become colored, especially of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a date or palm whose dates have begun to ripen, including the appearance of ripening at the part near the base or stalk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast a young one after its hair has grown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use of the she-camel; the more common competing expression uses سَبَّعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render benefits or boons complete, full, or ample to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal variant of أَسْبَغَ in the construction أَصْبَغَ اللهُ عليه النعم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become settled or established in religion, or to enter a good religious state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي الدِّينِ or صِبْغَةً حَسَنَةً.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become dyed or colored with something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The coloring material is introduced with بِـ or a related prepositional construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use a sauce, vinegar, or similar seasoning to make bread savory, or to prepare such a sauce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb describes using the seasoning with bread or making the seasoning itself; the source distinguishes this construction from directly making bread the object with vinegar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dye or coloring substance used for coloring clothes and similar objects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the ordinary material noun; it is distinct from the Quranic food-seasoning use of the same form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom حَدِيثَةُ الصِّبْغِ, a woman newly taken as a concubine or bride.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use apparently alluding to the recent application of henna dye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression بِصِبْغِ الثَّمَنِ, a price higher than the proper or cost price.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an idiom meaning that something was acquired for a raised price rather than its prime cost.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse whose whole fetlock is white without joining the whiteness of the leg marking called التَّحْجِيل.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine marking term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness at the extremity of the tail of a sheep, goat, or ewe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-coloration term corresponding to the epithet صَبْغَاء.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A date that has become ripe in part but not throughout.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for a partly ripened date.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of dyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The relational form is also attested as a designation for this occupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dyed; a dyed garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may also be used collectively of dyed garments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The craft or art of dyeing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Denotes the occupation or technical practice of the dyer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dyer of garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A liar or one who colors and alters information or discourse with falsehood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative extension from the dyer's coloring; also used in a reported saying about dyers and goldsmiths, with an alternative explanation based on broken promises.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel having a full udder of goodly color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Specialized description of a camel and its udder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels that put their heads into pasture or herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial description of camels feeding with their heads lowered into the pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a white marking in the forelock, tail, or ear; applied to horses, birds, and sheep or goats according to context.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The marking may be at an extremity or across the whole of the named part; the feminine صَبْغَاء is used especially of a dark sheep or goat with a white tail-tip.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of weak birds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who voids his excrement in his clothes when beaten or frightened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, specialized description applied to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert plant or grass with white fruit or with green upper portions and white shaded portions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers reported descriptions of a plant resembling panic grass and of a bunch of herbage showing this green-and-white contrast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The greatest or most powerful of torrents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized epithet used as a noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm tree whose dates are showing signs of ripening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized participial description of a palm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dye-house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun recorded in later or current usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dyed extensively or repeatedly; much dyed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The doubled form can indicate intensive application or application to many garments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that casts her young after its hair has grown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare participial use; مُسَبِّغ is reported as the more common form for this meaning.

cautions: صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ has several explicitly reported Quranic interpretations, including religion or fitrah and a baptismal reading; they are presented as distinct supported readings rather than collapsed into one exclusive translation.
The idiomatic صَبَغُونِي فِي عَيْنِكَ usage is disputed in the Classical evidence and may reflect confusion with صَبَعَ; it is retained only with that qualification.
